claim: All dietary supplement manufacturers in India must obtain an FSSAI license, and the product label must display the FSSAI license number prominently.
stance_target: FSSAI licensing is mandatory for Indian supplement brands including Briyo
scope_conditions: India, all dietary supplement manufacturers and importers
quoted_support: Manufacturers must confirm: That they have an existing FSSAI license for production or marketing... The FSSAI license number [must appear on the label].
entities: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

claim: FSSAI prohibits therapeutic claims on dietary supplement labels; all health-related statements must relate only to normal body functions and be backed by credible scientific research.
stance_target: Supplement brands in India cannot make disease-cure or treatment claims
quoted_support: The FSSAI does not permit: Therapeutic claims (for example 'cures arthritis'). Medical substitution claims (for example, 'a substitute for insulin'). Claims that lack scientific credibility, are exaggerated, or conflict with established facts are not permitted.

claim: FSSAI sets maximum ingredient limits per serving for specific nutrients: Vitamin A 10,000 IU, Iron 45 mg, Caffeine 200 mg, Theobromine 100 mg, L-Tryptophan 500 mg, Glucosamine 500 mg.
stance_target: FSSAI specifies ingredient dosage ceilings for dietary supplements
scope_conditions: India, per serving limits for dietary supplements
quoted_support: Vitamin A: 10,000 IU maximum per serving. Iron: 45 mg maximum per serving. L-Tryptophan: 500 mg maximum per serving. Glucosamine: 500 mg maximum per serving. Caffeine (Maximum allowable, 200 mg/serving) and theobromine (Max allowable 100 mg/serving).

claim: Dietary supplement labels in India must include batch number, expiry date, FSSAI license number, manufacturer name and address, usage instructions, and mandatory warning statements per the FSS (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020.
stance_target: FSSAI has specific mandatory labelling requirements for supplements sold in India
scope_conditions: India, per Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations 2020
quoted_support: The FSSAI license number [and] Batch number and expiry date [are required]. These provisions are in place to ensure transparency, traceability and informed use by consumers.
entities: Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations 2020

claim: Non-compliance with FSSAI regulations can result in financial penalties, product recall, loss of brand identity, and suspension or complete closure of manufacturing license.
stance_target: FSSAI has meaningful enforcement powers over non-compliant supplement brands
quoted_support: Depending on the type of non-compliance, the FSSAI may impose: Financial penalties/costs/fines. In cases involving safety risks, the product may be subject to recall procedures. Loss of brand identity. Suspension of license or complete closure (if serious).
